text:
Justin Brazeau scored against Boston on Nov. 5, the team where he became an NHL player, in only his second game of the season. He has one goal in three games and has played about 10 minutes a night.

Three games tells us almost nothing, and our on-ice numbers for him are noise at this sample. What we know is from last season: 17 goals and 34 points in 64 games, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 8.5 scoring chances per 60 minutes from the home-plate area in front of the net, the 99th percentile. That's his entire game: get to the crease and stay there. He also makes 21% of his setups from behind the net.

He is not fast. His skating sits at the bottom of our percentile scales, which is fine for a player whose office is six feet from the goal line. He's 28, undrafted, and came up through Providence. Evolving-Hockey had him 144th among 401 forwards last year. We project about 13 goals from here, assuming he gets regular minutes. Watch the ice time; 10 minutes isn't enough for a player like this.
headline: Brazeau back, and back at the net
